blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for houses that month.

blocks.text: Listings of houses in Chineside was little changed, 6 in June and 6 in October (+0.0%), and 2 sold across the 5 months. In October the community held 1.6% of Coquitlam’s 378 houses listed.
Chineside home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

10 houses sold in Chineside with a median price of $1,535,000 (the middle half sold between $1,468,450 and $1,576,625), taking a median of 12 days to sell at 95.8% of the last list price; 10% sold above list. They had a median $591 per square foot, a median year built of 1969 and a median lot of 8,646 square feet.

blocks.source: Source: Paragon, the MLS® system used by Jared’s office, closed sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026. Pending sales are not counted. Median means the middle price, so half sold for more and half for less. Sold vs list is the sale price as a percentage of the last list price. A figure is shown only where at least 5 homes sold, and a row is shown only with 5 or more sales; with fewer, one sale would be the whole figure.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Chineside?
